Commentary.Commentary: The Asian clash - The Rose Bowl in Southampton plays host to a richly contested rivalry, with Pakistan Women and Bangladesh Women locking horns. One side is desperate for their first win of this World Cup campaign, while the other is eager to return to winning ways after a recent stumble. Both teams arrive on the south-eastern coast of England with their semi-final hopes already teetering on the edge, knowing full well that anything less than victory here could prove fatal to their tournament aspirations. Pakistan stumble - Both Pakistan and Bangladesh arrived in England with modest ambitions and have so far been given brutal reality checks by the rest of Group 1. Pakistan opened their campaign with a 64-run thrashing at the hands of India in Birmingham, then collapsed to 50 for 8 against South Africa at Edgbaston before Fatima Sana's defiant fighting half-century dragged them to a fighting total, only for South Africa to chase it down with two wickets in hand. Two games, two defeats, zero points. Scars and survival - Bangladesh's story reads a little bit better. They were restricted to just 77 for 8 against Australia at Headingley, and then they were brushed aside by nine wickets inside ten overs, the kind of margin that leaves scars. But before that, they won their first match against the Dutch side, which might give them space to breathe. Team form (Last 5 completed WT20Is, recent first) - BAN-W - LWWWL | PAK-W - LLLLW. The shift in power - Here's a twist that may catch the casual fan off guard. Overall, Pakistan hold a commanding head-to-head record, winning 16 of the 20 completed T20I matches between the two sides. Yet since 2023, that dominance has all but evaporated, as Pakistan have managed just a single win in four encounters against Bangladesh. Most recent meeting did go Pakistan's way, a 31-run victory that saw Bangladesh restricted to 101/9 while chasing 133, but the broader recent trend tells a very different story. For a Bangladesh side desperate for any sliver of confidence after their last defeat, this is precisely the statistic their dressing room will be clinging to as they look to rediscover their winning touch.
